# Water cells join the constraint, both cities (instruction for Claude Code)

25 November 2026. My decision: cells whose majority Urban Atlas 2021 class is water (50000) are not eligible for greening and are excluded from the priority score, in both cities, with exactly the same majority class rule as the Malta airport and port constraint (spec 1.3). Klagenfurt gets a constraint for the first time (water only; there is still no airport in the study area).

```
Follow MCDA_paper_results_spec.md. Never use em dashes in any text you write (hyphens are fine).
For every comparison give both a figure and a table. Do not commit. Report first.

0. Checks
 - Grids: Malta 10,657 cells by gid; Klagenfurt 12,418 cells by ID. Stop if counts differ.

2. Define water cells with the same code path as the airport and port constraint: majority Urban Atlas 2021 class in the cell = 50000. One shared function for both cities.

 - Malta: constraint = airport and port (12400, 12300) or water (50000), majority class. Klagenfurt: constraint = water (50000), majority class.

4. Rerun everything that depends on the scores, both cities: scores, priority maps, Tables_MCDA, criterion maps, Step 3 (Burden_coincidence_random_weights.Rmd, with the 25 November tie rule and zero rule), and the full sensitivity set of spec 5.3.

5. Report, old (_pre_water) vs new, both cities:
 - eligible and scored cells; population in scored cells;
 - Spearman and top quintile overlap with the old score (over cells scored in both);
 - top 5 councils (Malta) or districts (Klagenfurt) with % of top quintile cells;
 - any normalisation bound that changed (criterion, old, new);
 - Step 3 main ratios (old: Malta 0.984, Klagenfurt 1.356);
 - citizen vs equal weights (Spearman, top quintile overlap);
 - maps: old vs new priority quintiles side by side;
 - paths of every new or changed file.
```
